### Quiescent Point Determination ($I_{\text{CQ}}$ and $V_{\text{CEQ}}$)
*(Data extracted from Fig: $V_{CC} = +20\text{ V}$, $V_{EE} = -20\text{ V}$ (total supply span $V_{CC}-V_{EE}=40\text{ V}$), $R_1 = 8.2\text{ k}\Omega$, $R_2 = 2.2\text{ k}\Omega$, $R_C = 2.7\text{ k}\Omega$, $R_E = 1.8\text{ k}\Omega$, $\beta = 120$)*

1. **DC Analysis - Thevenin Equivalent at Base:**
   - Thevenin voltage ($V_{TH}$):
     $$V_{TH} = V_{EE} + (V_{CC} - V_{EE}) \times \frac{R_2}{R_1 + R_2} = -20 + (40) \times \frac{2.2}{8.2 + 2.2} = -20 + 40(0.2115) = -11.54\text{ V}$|
   - Thevenin resistance ($R_{TH}$):
     $$R_{TH} = R_1 \parallel R_2 = \frac{8.2 \times 2.2}{10.4} = 1.73\text{ k}\Omega$$

2. **Base Current ($I_B$):**
   Applying KVL to the input loop:
   $$V_{TH} - I_B R_{TH} - V_{BE} - I_E R_E - V_{EE} = 0$$
   Since $I_E = (1 + \beta)I_B$:
   $$-11.54 - I_B(1.73\text{ k}\Omega) - 0.7 - (121)I_B(1.8\text{ k}\Omega) - (-20) = 0$$
   $$-11.54 - 0.7 + 20 - I_B(1.73 + 217.8)\text{ k}\Omega = 0$$
   $$7.76 - I_B(219.53\text{ k}\Omega) = 0 \implies I_B = \frac{7.76}{219.53\text{ k}\Omega} = 35.35\mu\text{A}$|

3. **Collector Current ($I_{\text{CQ}}$):**
   $$I_{\text{CQ}} = \beta I_B = 120 \times 35.35\mu\text{A} = 4.24\text{ mA}$|

4. **Collector-Emitter Voltage ($V_{\text{CEQ}}$):**
   Applying KVL across the output loop:
   $$V_{CC} - I_C R_C - V_{CE} - I_E R_E - V_{EE} = 0$$
   Assuming $I_E \approx I_C$:
   $$20 - (4.24\text{ mA})(2.7\text{ k}\Omega) - V_{\text{CEQ}} - (4.24\text{ mA})(1.8\text{ k}\Omega) - (-20) = 0$$
   $$20 - 11.45 - V_{\text{CEQ}} - 7.63 + 20 = 0$$
   $$V_{\text{CEQ}} = 40 - 19.08 = 20.92\text{ V}$|
proTip: When dual power supplies ($V_{CC}$ and $V_{EE}$) are used, always account for $V_{EE}$ properly in the base-bias and collector-emitter KVL equations.
